seoTitle: How to Find NASDAQ in TradingView Correctly
metaDescription: Learn how to search and select the correct NASDAQ symbol in TradingView, understand NASDAQ Composite vs NAS100 vs futures, and set up your chart.
intro: Searching 'NASDAQ' in TradingView can surface several similar symbols, and choosing the wrong one can throw off your analysis. This guide explains how to find the correct NASDAQ symbol, the difference between the NASDAQ Composite, NAS100, and NASDAQ futures, and how to pick the right data source. It's aimed at stock and index traders who want accurate charts from the start.

steps.heading: Understand what NASDAQ means in TradingView
steps.body: NASDAQ can refer to the exchange itself or to specific indices tracking groups of stocks listed on it, so context matters when searching.

steps.heading: Search NASDAQ in TradingView
steps.body: Use the symbol search bar and type NASDAQ to see the various matching index and futures symbols available.

steps.heading: Choose the correct symbol
steps.body: Select between the NASDAQ Composite, NAS100, or NASDAQ futures depending on what specific instrument you want to analyze.

steps.heading: Understand Composite vs NAS100 vs futures
steps.body: The Composite tracks a broad set of NASDAQ-listed stocks, NAS100 focuses on the largest non-financial companies, and futures track the derivative contract.

steps.heading: Apply best chart settings for analyzing NASDAQ
steps.body: Once you've selected the right symbol, configure your timeframe and chart style based on whether you're doing intraday or longer-term analysis.

faq.question: What's the difference between NASDAQ Composite and NAS100?
faq.answer: The NASDAQ Composite includes a broad range of NASDAQ-listed companies, while NAS100 typically tracks the 100 largest non-financial companies on the exchange.

faq.question: Should I use NASDAQ futures for intraday trading?
faq.answer: Many intraday traders prefer futures data because it trades outside regular market hours, unlike the cash index which only reflects official trading hours.

faq.question: Why do multiple NASDAQ symbols appear when I search?
faq.answer: Different data providers and exchanges list NASDAQ-related instruments under slightly different symbols, which is why several options show up in search.

faq.question: Does the data source affect the NASDAQ price shown?
faq.answer: Yes, different providers can show slightly different prices depending on how they calculate or feed the index or futures data.
